questions: The board carries no node yet for any of the astronauts, officials and ministers this topic is meant to hold: Edgar Mitchell, Gordon Cooper, Paul Hellyer, Haim Eshed, Lord Hill-Norton, or the 2013 Citizen Hearing. Which of them should be admitted first?

For each, what written or parliamentary record fixes when the claim was made? The stub names two, Cooper's 1978 letter to the United Nations and Hellyer's record in Hansard; what are the equivalents for the others?
For each, did the person claim first-hand knowledge, or repeat what others told them, and who were those others?
What had each of them said before being contacted by an interested party or an organised disclosure effort, and were any of them given another witness's account first?
Where their accounts overlap, do they agree on substance while differing on detail, or do they repeat the same wording, which would point to a shared source?
Who testified at the 2013 Citizen Hearing, who organised and selected the witnesses, and how many of them were first collected by the same interviewer?
